claims.text: The starting feedstock is pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder with a particle-size distribution typical of LPBF.
Approximately 0.5–1 vol% nanoscale Y2O3 can be homogeneously dispersed into metallic additive-manufacturing powder.
Adding 0.5–1 vol% nanoscale Y2O3 to AlCrFeNiSi feedstock is an effective intervention for miniature LPBF components.
Y2O3 nanoparticles mitigate high thermal gradients during LPBF.
Moderate laser power and scan speed can minimize extreme melt-pool temperatures while retaining near-full densification.
The proposed processing window applies to sub-10 mm miniature components.
Uniformly distributed Y2O3 nanoparticles act as heterogeneous nucleation sites in the AlCrFeNiSi melt pool.
Nanoparticle-assisted nucleation interrupts the formation of large columnar grains.
Nanoparticle-assisted nucleation promotes a refined, equiaxed microstructure.
An equiaxed microstructure reduces the buildup of residual thermal stress.
Y2O3 nanoparticles modify melt-pool dynamics by enhancing local heat dissipation.
Grain refinement reduces the thermal gradients experienced during processing.
Reduced thermal gradients lower residual-stress accumulation.
Y2O3 modification will increase tensile strength relative to conventional high-thermal-load LPBF processing.
Y2O3 modification will increase ductility relative to conventional high-thermal-load LPBF processing.
The modified components will have measurably lower residual thermal stress than unmodified components made by high-thermal-load LPBF.
The anticipated benefits may not transfer to larger geometries or substantially different process conditions without parameter adjustment.
Failure to achieve about a 15% residual-stress reduction and a 10% increase in tensile strength and/or ductility constitutes falsification.

contradictions.description: The modified specimens are prescribed a moderate-energy process window, while the baseline is defined as conventional high-thermal-load LPBF; however, the falsification experiment requires identical laser power, scan speed, hatch spacing, and other parameters for both groups. The experiment therefore cannot simultaneously implement both stated processing regimes.
